messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] Pomoč pri statistični analizi podatkov_podobnost med lokacijama
parts:
Hoj!

Switching to English as I know that Maarten has been dealing with species richness metrics and he may be willing to add something.

I've just stumbled into a similar problem in genetics where a solution from ecological literature is used. So, one way to compare species richness in both locations is rarefaction - I'm attaching the Hurlbert's 1971 classic paper on the topic. There may be an R package or other software out there that can do the calculations for you, but I've never dealt with this for ecological data.

The more R friendly way (and quite unavailable for Hurlbert & Co. in the early 1970's) is to do multiple bootstrap-like resampling. This is easy to do in R. First you will need to transform your data so that you have a different data frame for each location, and one record (row) for each occurence of each species. Then you randomly resample the data from the location with more data (in your case location 1) to the sample size of location 2. Do this many times (about 10000 should be ok), and calculate the mean and standard deviation of your number of species over all subsamples. Following the central limit theorem this should follow the normal distribution, so you can do a simple Z-test to see if the number of species seen at location 2 could be expected if the actual number of species is the same as in location 1.

Will you be able to handle this?

Cheers,

Tomaz

parts:
Dear Petra,

Total communities can be analysed using Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling
(NMDS) (MASS package) based on Bray-Curtis similarity matrix to present the
differences/similarities in the community structure.


Additionally take a look at vegan package for analysing multivariate data
sets with biological data.

Sincerely,
Andreja
